note:
57 -> 52, banked once, at the end of the branch that earned it.

Measured the same way at both ends -- detached worktrees with node_modules
symlinked, no uncommitted work in either -- so the delta is attributable:

    801a6773577 (merge-base)   57, matching the floor it carried
    HEAD (all source work in)  52

The -5 by name. Three are the core refactor, which is what this floor had been
waiting on longest:

    228  core/assets.js        loadESMBundle
    132  core/network/rpc.js   _rpc, the four-way router
    110  core/network/rpc.js   the fetch continuation

and two are the list work -- computeAggregates (176 lines, six jobs and five
flags threaded between them) and useDynamicPlaceholder (98, with
buildPlaceholderText and insertAtRange lifted out). view.js, list_grid_state.js,
form_compiler.js and column_width_hook.js also shortened but were already inside
the 90-line budget.

WHY THIS GATE KEEPS GOING RED, WRITTEN DOWN SO THE NEXT PERSON DOES NOT REDISCOVER
IT. This floor moves whenever anyone shortens a long function, which is exactly
what it exists to encourage, and the mode is `exact`, so an improvement fails the
build in the same way a regression does. A commit that shortens one must carry the
new number or hand the next person a red gate they did not cause. Nothing enforces
that.

The failure mode with the sign flipped is just as costly and is what CLAUDE.md §5
recorded here: banking against a working tree that carried someone else's
uncommitted improvement, so the floor sat below what any clean checkout measures.
A worktree is only a clean reading if the number it is compared against comes from
one too. That entry is resolved by this commit -- the work it was measuring is now
committed, and a clean worktree and the working tree both read 52.
